newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols stay bid ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols stay bid ahead of data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options remained well bid in late trade as the market awaited retail sales and inflation data due out in the coming days, traders said.
The underlying Treasury bond market, still shaky after Friday's selloff, shed early gains in the afternoon and slipped into negative territory toward the close.

Brad Tyl, Aubrey G Lanston's floor manager at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT), said bidding was stronger in the front months, causing an inversion in the volatility curve in the September-December portion.

"It shows a great deal of anxiety before major (data) releases," Tyl said, adding this could be confirmation the market's four-month rally had run its course and concerns over a Federal Reserve tightening was growing.
"It's what they used to do prior to starting this trend higher in the bonds," he said of the volatility curve inversion. "They hadn't done it in the last two months, which is indicative of a trend."
Shorter dated options have higher gamma, which provides quicker premium acceleration as well as bigger delta swings for volatility traders against bond price movements.
